items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: Well, anyway, Manzi once played a job with Wilton Crawley.

ctx.x: I think with a Z. I thought so, too.

Bob thought it was an S. He's gone now. Okay. Well, anyway, Manzi once played a job with Wilton Crawley. Wilton Crawley recorded quite a few jelly songs, about four or six, I forget what they are. And Crawley had his own band, of course, sometimes used some of Lou Russell's band. But they played a date out at some insane asylum, I guess you'd call it, out on Long Island. And some of the guards were responsible from the different buildings to take a certain bunch of the patients, you know, in the little bus. So…
He said, I'm Wilton Crawley, the world's greatest clarinet player.
